items.followUp: Write HTML code to display the text “Welcome” in font size 6.

items.followUp: Write two characteristics of bus topology.

rubric.why: A star network connects each device to a central device.
rubric.description: State that all devices connect to a central hub or switch.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the central connection point.

rubric.why: A second characteristic may describe a benefit or limitation of star topology.
rubric.description: Give another correct characteristic of star topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a distinct correct characteristic.

modelAnswer: Each computer or device is connected to a central hub or switch.
If the central hub fails, communication between the connected devices stops.

rubric.why: File sharing involves making files available to others.
rubric.description: State that file sharing means making files available to other users or computers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the idea of making files available to others.

rubric.why: Files are shared so other users can access or transfer them, often over a network.
rubric.description: Mention access to or transfer of files between users or computers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct means or purpose of sharing files.

modelAnswer: File sharing is the process of making files available to other users or computers.
Users can access or transfer shared files, often over a network.

rubric.description: State the IPv4 dotted-decimal format.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying four dot-separated numbers.

rubric.why: The answer must give a valid example of an IPv4 address.
rubric.description: Give a valid IPv4 example.

items.followUp: Define an algorithm and write two advantages and two disadvantages of using one.

rubric.why: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of steps for solving a problem.
rubric.description: Define an algorithm as a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition conveying the steps and problem-solving purpose.

rubric.why: Algorithms have advantages such as clarity, language independence, and helping detect errors.
rubric.description: Give three correct advantages of algorithms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for three distinct correct advantages.

rubric.why: Algorithms can take time to write and may become lengthy or difficult for complex problems.
rubric.description: Give three correct disadvantages of algorithms.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for three distinct correct disadvantages; award 1 mark for one or two.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step set of instructions used to solve a problem.
Advantages:
It is easy to understand and communicate.
It is independent of any programming language.
It helps identify errors in the solution before coding.
Disadvantages:
Writing an algorithm can be time-consuming.
An algorithm for a large problem can become lengthy.
It may be difficult to write or follow for a complex problem.

items.followUp: Name the four layers of the TCP/IP model and briefly state the function of each.

rubric.why: TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol.
rubric.description: Give the expansion or identify TCP/IP as the protocol suite.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct expansion or identification.

rubric.why: The application layer provides network services to applications.
rubric.description: Name the application layer and state its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the layer name and a correct function.

rubric.why: The transport layer manages end-to-end communication and delivery.
rubric.description: Name the transport layer and state its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the layer name and a correct function.

rubric.why: The internet layer handles addressing and routing, while the network access layer sends data over the physical network.
rubric.description: Name and describe the internet and network access layers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying both lower layers and their general functions.

modelAnswer: TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol; it is a suite of protocols used for communication over networks.
The Application layer provides network services to applications and users.
The Transport layer manages end-to-end communication and delivery of data.
The Internet layer handles logical addressing and routing of packets between networks.
The Network Access layer sends and receives data over the physical network medium.

items.followUp: Write a short note on phishing and identity theft as cybercrimes.

rubric.why: Hacking involves gaining unauthorised access to a computer or network.
rubric.description: Describe hacking as unauthorised access to systems or data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of hacking.

rubric.why: Malware or virus attacks can damage systems or data.
rubric.description: Describe a virus or malware attack.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying malicious software and its harmful effect.

rubric.why: Phishing tricks people into revealing sensitive information, often through fake messages or websites.
rubric.description: Describe phishing or another information-stealing cybercrime.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example and explanation.

rubric.why: Online harassment or identity theft is another common type of cybercrime.
rubric.description: Describe cyberstalking, online harassment, or identity theft.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct type of cybercrime and its basic meaning.

modelAnswer: Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to a computer system or network.
A virus or malware attack uses harmful software to damage a computer or its data.
Phishing uses fake emails or websites to trick people into giving passwords or other personal information.
Cyberstalking is using the internet to harass or threaten a person; identity theft involves using another person’s personal information to impersonate them.
